profile.campus: Lumen / Level 3 Texas Triangle (Dallas / Austin / San Antonio)
profile.reading:
This Lumen colocation facility is located at 3180 Irving Blvd, Dallas, TX 75247, a separate building from the nearby Regal Row Lumen Dallas 6 facility also tracked in this registry; Lumen does not publish individual building addresses or specs on its own site for any of its 175-plus North American colocation sites. Lumen Technologies, formerly CenturyLink (renamed Lumen on September 14, 2020, with its stock ticker changing from CTL to LUMN on September 18, 2020) and built in part on CenturyLink's November 1, 2017 acquisition of Level 3 Communications, operates this facility as part of a network-centric edge colocation product rather than a wholesale hyperscale campus. Lumen's own colocation data sheet states more than 175 carrier-neutral data centers across more than 60 North American markets, offering cabinet power in the 3 to 15 kilowatt range described as varying by site; unlike the wholesale operators tracked elsewhere in this registry, Lumen does not disclose per-building square footage or total MW capacity for any of its sites.

Texas's data center sales tax exemption cost the state roughly $5-30 million a year from 2014 through 2022, jumped to more than $150 million in 2023, and is now projected at $1.3 billion for the current fiscal year, $3.2 billion over 2026-2028, and nearly $1.8 billion annually by fiscal 2030, according to the Texas Tribune. Separately, ERCOT's interconnection queue holds roughly 474 gigawatts of pending requests, more than five times the grid's record peak demand, with Governor Abbott stating about 90% of new power requests are data centers; Abbott ordered an audit of queued data centers in August 2026, and ERCOT sought a delay of its transmission planning study from the Public Utility Commission the same month.

Dallas' Irving Boulevard/Regal Row corridor has served as a telecommunications and colocation hub for decades, predating the newer hyperscale campuses further out in Garland and other Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Lumen operates a data center at 3180 Irving Boulevard in Dallas, Texas, but the facility's power capacity and customer load are not publicly disclosed.

Lumen inherited this site through a complex corporate history. The company was originally founded in 1930, acquired Level 3 Communications in 2017, then divested most of its data center portfolio to Cyxtera Technologies in the same year while retaining roughly 10 percent equity and separate colocation operations. The registry cannot determine whether this specific Dallas facility was part of the 2017 divestiture or remained under Lumen control. The company's current colocation offerings claim over 200 North American locations, but facility-by-facility records of the asset split remain unavailable.

Without published capacity data, this facility's contribution to either Lumen's infrastructure or regional AI compute availability cannot be quantified. The data confirms a physical address and operator, establishing that colocation infrastructure exists in Dallas, but says nothing about how much power it draws, how much is allocated to AI workloads, or how fully it is utilized. Researchers seeking to understand Texas data center capacity face a broader constraint: most operators do not disclose load or available power in their public profiles.
